newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - July 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - July 21.

-- NATIONWIDE PREPARE FOR CRUCIAL VOTE

Nationwide building society is seeking legal advice on the early release on Wednesday of the results of the board elections, which pits five board nominees against activists wishing the society to demutualise. The society is holding its AGM on Thursday and to deter results-seeking crowds of members it plans the early release of the election results which will determine its future as a 'mutual' member-owned society or as a demutualised building society that will give members a windfall pay-off.
-- US COULD RETALIATE IF BRUSSELS REJECTS BOEING BID

Six US government agencies are prepared to impose restrictions on flights between France and the US if the European Commission rejects the proposed merger between US aircraft manufacturers Boeing and McDonnell Douglas. France is vulnerable to proposed retaliation because it has no formal flight arrangements with the US but if Brussels disapproves the merger on Wednesday as expected it could impose sanctions by levying fines and impounding aircraft.
-- COMPANIES PLAN PENSIONS RETHINK AFTER TAX CHANGE

Accountants Arthur Andersen suggest that many big British companies may move away from final salary pension schemes following the governments budget decision to scrap tax credits on dividends. A survey revealed that many firms may opt to introduce defined contribution or money purchase schemes which may mean that employees can longer solely rely on company pensions and may have to take out additional saving.
-- COMPANIES MAY OFFER SLIMMER FINANCIAL SUMMARIES

Demutualised building societies, the Halifax, Woolwich and Alliance and Leicester, announced plans to save millions by sending shareholders slimmer summarised annual financial reports instead of traditional profit and loss accounts that can be given upon request. The user-friendly summary financial statements may spell the end for traditional heavy accounts.
-- ONE OFF BOOST FOR FRANCE TELECOM

State-owned France Telecom, which is to traded on the New York Stock Exchange later in the year, is expected to announce a one-off item boost to 1997 profits of FFr1.3bn following the 7.75 per cent stake sale of Cofira, the Cegetel subsidiary, rival company to Telecom in the new open telecom market. Trading in France Telecom shares has been delayed following the unexpected general election victory of the Socialist party which will hope to raise between FFr30bn and FFr50bn from the sale.
-- DELAY OVER EURO 'WOULD BRING THREAT OF DAMAGES'

Mr Yves-Thibault de Silguy, European Union commissioner responsible for monetary affairs warned that if the EU heads of government postpone the start of the single currency beyond the 1999 date it would be a breach of the 1992 Maastricht treaty for economic and monetary union which would allow all banks and companies to pursue damages claims for costs incurred.
-- EURO WARNING FOR UK GROUPS

Barclays Bank have warned companies in the UK whether or not they join Emu in 1999, they may have to switch billing and payment systems from sterling to euros. Bankers state UK companies which trade within the Union may pass on their own currency exposure to their UK-based suppliers, creating a 'knock- on' effect for the euro within the country. Siemens UK finance director Bernd Euler added 'the more the euro gains momentum, the bigger will be its impact and the more UK suppliers will have to adjust'.
-- BT CHIEF DUE IN US TO DISCUSS MCI DEAL

Sir Peter Bonfield, British Telecom's chief executive is to fly to MCI's main office in Washington on Monday to speak with MCI directors on the future of the merger between the two groups. Over the weekend, Sir Peter was in consultation with BT finance director Robert Brace, MCI chairman Bert Roberts and MCI chief executive Gerald Taylor, reviewing his options for the deal, currently valued at about $45 per share.
-- GERMANY SEEMS UNLIKELY TO HALT D-MARK'S SLIDE

The D-Mark, long decreasing in value, has entered a recent nosedive which has seen its value plunge 15 pfennigs against the pound in the last month and over five pfennigs against the dollar in the last two weeks. As it appears the country is doing little to end the decline - chancellor Kohl has labelled the news 'not earth shattering' - the forex market has predicted that in 18 months, the D-Mark will merge into a weak Emu.
-- GLAXO'S HIGH HOPES FOR DIABETES DRUG

Clinical evidence for troglitazone, the diabetes drug joint- developed by Glaxo Wellcome, Warner-Lambert and Sankyo, will be presented before the International Diabetic Conference this week, amid analysts predictions the drug will create a global market worth over 1bn stg per year. The three companies will show that treatment with their drug decreases the risk of heart and kidney failure, the leading causes of death among diabetes patients. Troglitazone is aimed at those with Type 2 forms of the disease, amounting to some 90 per cent of all cases.
